name: hcapp_authorizeDevice
description: First-time device registration (sign-in with an invite code, or by @userId from a flow that already knows the hasher). Pre-auth endpoint: the token is validated with HC.CHECK_ACCESS_TOKEN_V2 against the null user UUID and a fixed 30 s window (1102 / errorType 11). Resolves the hasher by @userId, else by @scanText = Hasher.ResetCode ('URC:…') → 1302 not found (13); a removed hasher → 1402 (14). Generates a 75-character uppercase base64 DeviceSecret (CRYPT_GEN_RANDOM) and a TimeWindow of 30-44 s, then in one transaction: Hasher.LastLoginDateTime/HcVersion/updatedAt; a LaunchAndLogin row carrying DeviceId and the five device fields (from the optional parameters, else from @deviceData JSON, 2026-10-12); DELETE + INSERT of the HC.Device row (idempotent re-registration) with IsMobile, Version, BuildNumber and Locale. Returns the hasher profile joined to the new device row, including deviceSecret and timeWindow — the credentials every later token is generated from. The whole body, including the auth check, is inside TRY/CATCH (1902 / 19). @isMobile = 0 marks a browser (E9.F7): no push tokens, not counted as a phone. Idempotent writes (2026-10-14, audit W4), row 'creates a row': a BROWSER repeat — @isMobile = 0 and an HC.Device row with the same @deviceId already exists for the SAME user, IsMobile = 0, removed = 0, SignedOutAt NULL and updatedAt within the last 2 minutes (checked WITH (UPDLOCK, HOLDLOCK) inside the transaction) — writes nothing (no Hasher update, no LaunchAndLogin row, no DELETE/INSERT) and returns the existing deviceSecret and timeWindow as success. The web mints its deviceId once per sign-in flow (signed hc_signin cookie) so a double submit or a retry after a lost reply is that repeat. Every other case, including every @isMobile = 1 (app) call, which neither takes the lock nor the branch, is unchanged: DELETE + INSERT with a freshly rotated secret.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Client-generated device UUID. Used as the PK for the new Device record. Expected to be generated once per app install and stable across re-registrations.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Global shared access token. Validated via HC.CHECK_ACCESS_TOKEN_V2 against the null user UUID (00000000-...). This is a pre-auth endpoint — no per-user token is available yet.

parameters.name: hcVersion
parameters.description: App version string e.g. '3.0.0'. Stored on Hasher.HcVersion. Narrowed from NVARCHAR(250) in HC5 to match the NVARCHAR(50) column definition.

parameters.name: scanText
parameters.description: User invite code in 'URC:XXXXXX' format. Used to look up the hasher when @userId is not provided. Mutually exclusive with @userId — one must be supplied. When @userId is provided, this parameter is overwritten internally with the user's actual ResetCode (used only for error log context).

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Direct user lookup by Hasher.id. When provided, @scanText is ignored for the lookup.

parameters.name: deviceData
parameters.description: JSON blob of device metadata (OS, browser name, etc.). Stored as-is in Device.DeviceData. The OperatingSystem computed column on Device is derived from this JSON.

parameters.name: apnsToken
parameters.description: Apple Push Notification Service token. NULL for Android devices.

parameters.name: fcmToken
parameters.description: Firebase Cloud Messaging token. NULL for iOS-only installs that have not granted FCM permission.

parameters.name: isMobile
parameters.description: 1 (default) phone app; 0 browser signing in with an emailed code (E9.F7). Added 2026-09-16, optional, non-breaking.

parameters.name: buildNumber
parameters.description: App build number, e.g. '1470'. Optional (2026-10-12); with it HcVersion on the login row is 'HC Ver: x, Bld: n' and the device row gets Version/BuildNumber at once.

parameters.name: deviceType
parameters.description: Device model string, as hcapp_approveLogin takes it. Optional; falls back to the model in @deviceData.

parameters.name: deviceName
parameters.description: User-assigned device name. Optional; falls back to @deviceData.

parameters.name: systemName
parameters.description: OS name, e.g. 'iOS'. Optional; falls back to @deviceData.

parameters.name: systemVersion
parameters.description: OS version. Optional; falls back to @deviceData.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: Device locale, e.g. 'en_GB'. Optional; '' when absent.

rowsets.name: StatusEnvelope
rowsets.description: Always returned as the first rowset. success=1 means the operation succeeded and rowset 1 is the HasherProfile. success=0 means failure and rowset 1 is an error detail row. errorCode encodes the failure class (1102=auth, 1302=not found, 1402=removed, 1902=db error). errorType maps to HC6 error classification (11=auth token invalid, 13=not found, 14=removed/restricted, 19=unhandled DB error).

columns.name: success
columns.description: 1 on success, 0 on any error path.

columns.name: errorCode
columns.description: NULL on success. On failure: 1102=invalid access token, 1302=invite code/user not found, 1402=account removed, 1902=unhandled DB error.

columns.name: errorType
columns.description: NULL on success. On failure: 11=auth token invalid, 13=not found, 14=removed/restricted, 19=unhandled DB error.

rowsets.name: HasherProfile
rowsets.description: Returned when success=1. Full hasher profile joined with the newly created device record. Contains the device credentials (deviceSecret, timeWindow) required for all subsequent CHECK_ACCESS_TOKEN_V2 calls.

columns.name: displayName
columns.description: Hasher.DisplayName — persisted computed column (hash name or full name based on NameDisplayPreference). Falls back to '<no names provided>' if neither is set.

columns.name: qrSecretCode
columns.description: Hasher.QR_secret_code — secret UUID used for QR verification.

columns.name: includeInGlobalHashDirectory
columns.description: Hasher.IncludeInGlobalHashDirectory — whether this hasher appears in the global directory.

columns.name: thirdPartyForceTokenRefresh
columns.description: Hasher.ThirdPartyForceTokenRefresh — signals the app to refresh its OAuth token.

columns.name: deviceSecret
columns.description: Device.DeviceSecret — cryptographically random 75-character secret (uppercase base64, + and / stripped). Used by the app to generate short-lived auth tokens for all subsequent CHECK_ACCESS_TOKEN_V2 calls. Renamed from 'iconDataBase64' in HC5.

columns.name: timeWindow
columns.description: Device.TimeWindow — TOTP-style token validity window in seconds, randomly chosen between 30 and 44 at registration. Used alongside deviceSecret for token generation. Renamed from 'colorPaletteIndex' in HC5.

rowsets.name: ErrorDetail
rowsets.description: Returned when success=0. Contains a single error detail row corresponding to the failure captured in rowset 0. The errorId references the HC.ErrorLog entry created for this failure.

columns.name: errorId
columns.description: GUID of the HC.ErrorLog entry created for this failure.

columns.name: errorType
columns.description: Same value as in the StatusEnvelope: 11=auth token invalid, 13=not found, 14=removed/restricted, 19=unhandled DB error.

columns.name: errorCode
columns.description: Same value as in the StatusEnvelope: 1102, 1302, 1402, or 1902.

columns.name: errorTitle
columns.description: Short error title for display: 'Invalid access token', 'Invite code not found', 'Account removed', or 'Unexpected error'.

columns.name: errorUserMessage
columns.description: Full user-facing error message explaining next steps.

sideEffects: UPDATE HC.Hasher SET LastLoginDateTime = GETDATE(), HcVersion = @hcVersion, updatedAt = GETDATE() WHERE id = @userId

INSERT HC.LaunchAndLogin (HcVersion = 'HC Ver: x, Bld: n' when @buildNumber is sent else @hcVersion, UserId, UserName = '~name~', DeviceId, DeviceType, DeviceName, SystemName, SystemVersion, Manufacturer — the five from the parameters, else JSON_VALUE of @deviceData with iOS/Android key fallbacks)
DELETE FROM HC.Device WHERE id = @deviceId — idempotent prior-record cleanup, correct for all platforms including Android

INSERT INTO HC.Device (id, DeviceSecret, TimeWindow, DeviceData, UserId, ApnsToken, FcmToken, IsMobile, Version = LEFT(@hcVersion, 25) when @buildNumber is sent else '<unknown>', BuildNumber = COALESCE(@buildNumber, '<unknown>'), Locale = COALESCE(@locale, ''))
INSERT HC.ErrorLog on auth failure, not-found, removed-user, and DB error paths
All writes (Hasher UPDATE, LaunchAndLogin INSERT, Device DELETE+INSERT) are wrapped in a single transaction and rolled back on error
Browser repeat (@isMobile = 0, same device + user, IsMobile 0, live, updatedAt < 2 min old): NO writes — the existing HC.Device secret and time window are returned (2026-10-14, audit W4)

codeSmells.detail: @deviceId, @accessToken, @hcVersion, @deviceData (lines 3, 4, 5 and 8) have no SQL default. A client that omits any of them is refused by SQL BEFORE the procedure runs: no HC.ErrorLog row, an empty 500 in the app, and the SP's own graceful checks are unreachable (CLAUDE.md, Rack of Lamb 2026-09-29). Note @deviceData sits AFTER two defaulted parameters, so a positional caller cannot skip @scanText/@userId.

codeSmells.issue: Device.LastLogin not explicitly set on re-registration
codeSmells.detail: HC.Device.LastLogin has a DEFAULT of GETDATE(), so it is set correctly on INSERT. However the column name implies it should be updated on every login, not just first registration. A separate update-login SP would be needed for this, or LastLogin should be removed from Device in favour of HC.LaunchAndLogin.

codeSmells.issue: timeWindow upper bound is 44, not 45 as documented
codeSmells.detail: CAST((RAND() * 15) + 30 AS INT) produces values from 30 to 44 inclusive (RAND() returns [0,1), so the maximum before truncation is 44.999...). The SP header comment says '30-45' — the upper bound is off by one. Not a correctness issue in practice but worth noting for any client-side validation.

codeSmells.issue: Device.Version stays '<unknown>' when an older app omits @buildNumber even though @hcVersion is known
codeSmells.detail: Line 238 writes LEFT(@hcVersion, 25) only when @buildNumber IS NOT NULL; an app that sends @hcVersion but not @buildNumber still gets Version '<unknown>' until its next hcapp_approveLogin.

breakingChanges: @hcVersion narrowed from NVARCHAR(250) to NVARCHAR(50) to match Hasher.HcVersion column — callers passing version strings longer than 50 characters will receive a parameter truncation error at the SP boundary
Success rowset column 'iconDataBase64' renamed to 'deviceSecret' — all Flutter app parsing code reading this column by name must be updated
Success rowset column 'colorPaletteIndex' renamed to 'timeWindow' — all Flutter app parsing code reading this column by name must be updated
Removed-user path now returns errorType=14 (was errorType=5 in HC5) — callers that switch on errorType to detect account-removed state must be updated
Not-found path now returns errorType=13 (was errorType=5 in HC5) — callers that switch on errorType to detect not-found state must be updated
Auth failure path now returns a two-rowset response (StatusEnvelope + ErrorDetail) matching the write SP envelope pattern — was a single ad-hoc rowset in HC5
DeviceSecret is now stored and returned as uppercase (UPPER() applied) — was mixed-case in HC5; any client comparison against a cached copy of the secret must account for the case change

Device cleanup DELETE now targets the specific @deviceId (was a buggy ApnsToken+FcmToken AND-match in HC5) — behaviour change for re-registration: the old record for the same device UUID is always removed, regardless of push token values
